steps.title: Skeleton & health check
steps.goal: A running FastAPI app with GET /health returning JSON.
concepts: ASGI server (uvicorn) vs framework (FastAPI): the server speaks HTTP, the framework routes requests to your functions.
A health endpoint is what load balancers, ECS and Kubernetes poll. Keep it cheap: no database calls.
FastAPI generates OpenAPI docs for free at /docs (Swagger UI) and /openapi.json.
App factory pattern (create_app) so tests can build isolated instances.

steps.title: CRUD on a resource
steps.goal: Create, read, list, partially update and delete observations, with correct status codes.
concepts: Resources are nouns (/observations); HTTP methods are the verbs.
POST creates -> 201 Created + Location header pointing at the new resource.
PATCH changes some fields; PUT replaces the whole resource. PUT and DELETE are idempotent, POST is not.
DELETE -> 204 No Content (empty body). Reading it afterwards -> 404.
Document store: each observation is one JSON document (TinyDB here; MongoDB/DynamoDB in production).

checks.name: GET the Location URL returns it
GET list filtered by station finds exactly 1
PATCH changes only the sent field

steps.title: Validation & consistent errors
steps.goal: Reject bad input with 422, missing things with 404, duplicates with 409, all in one error shape.
concepts: Validate at the edge: Pydantic models declare types, ranges and patterns once.
400 malformed request, 404 not found, 409 conflicts with current state, 422 well-formed but invalid.
One error envelope {error: {code, message, details}} so clients parse one format.
Never return stack traces to clients; log them server-side instead.

checks.name: Unknown id -> 404 in the error envelope

steps.title: Filtering & pagination
steps.goal: List endpoints that never return unbounded results.
concepts: Query parameters filter and page a collection: ?station=KJFK&since=...&limit=20&offset=40.
Always cap limit (here 100). An unbounded list endpoint is an outage waiting to happen.
Offset paging is simple but slow on deep pages and shifts when rows are inserted; cursor (keyset) paging fixes both.
Return paging metadata (total, limit, offset) with the items.

steps.title: Authentication & authorization
steps.goal: API keys in the X-API-Key header; reads are public, writes need a read-write key.
concepts: 401 = who are you? (missing/invalid credentials). 403 = I know you, and you're not allowed.
A 401 should carry a WWW-Authenticate header naming the scheme.
Compare secrets with secrets.compare_digest (constant time).
Keys only travel safely over HTTPS (step 10). In production: keys in AWS Secrets Manager, or OAuth2/JWT, or API Gateway + Cognito/IAM.

checks.name: GET without a key is allowed (public reads)

steps.title: Rate limiting
steps.goal: Token-bucket limits per API key (generous) and per IP for anonymous clients (strict).
concepts: Token bucket: capacity = allowed burst, refill rate = sustained requests/second.
Exceeded -> 429 Too Many Requests + Retry-After (seconds). Well-behaved clients back off with exponential backoff + jitter.
X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining headers let clients pace themselves.
Only valid keys get their own bucket; otherwise clients could rotate fake keys to dodge the limit.
In-memory buckets don't work across several instances: use Redis, or API Gateway usage plans / AWS WAF rate rules.

checks.name: 15 fast anonymous requests hit 429 + Retry-After
checks.hint: Anonymous limit defaults to a burst of 10, refilling 1/s. The check waits a few seconds afterwards so later checks aren't throttled.

steps.title: WebSockets (server push)
steps.goal: Clients on /ws/observations receive every new observation as it's created.
concepts: A WebSocket starts as an HTTP GET with Upgrade: websocket; the server answers 101 Switching Protocols and the TCP connection stays open, full duplex.
Use it when the server needs to push (live feeds). Alternatives: polling, long-polling, Server-Sent Events (one-way, plain HTTP).
ws:// is plain, wss:// is WebSocket over TLS (same certs as HTTPS).
Handle disconnects: a dead client must not break the broadcast for everyone else.
Several server instances? Each only knows its own sockets, so fan out through Redis pub/sub, SNS/SQS, or API Gateway WebSocket APIs.

checks.name: Creating an observation pushes observation.created to WS clients

steps.title: C++ core via ctypes
steps.goal: Flight category and wind components computed by a C++ shared library called from Python.
concepts: extern "C" turns off C++ name mangling so ctypes can find functions by name.
Only C types cross the boundary: ints, doubles, char*, pointers. No std::string, no exceptions.
Always set argtypes/restype in ctypes. Without them, floats raise ArgumentError, ints are passed where C expects doubles (garbage results), and returned pointers are truncated to ints.
Out-parameters: pass ctypes.byref(c_double()) and C writes into it.
The library's bitness/ABI must match Python: 64-bit Python can't load a 32-bit DLL (WinError 193).
Alternatives: pybind11 / nanobind (C++ classes, exceptions), Cython, CFFI, or a separate process.

checks.name: Server reports engine=cpp (library loaded)
checks.hint: Build the library (native\build.bat on Windows, native/build.sh on Linux/macOS) and restart uvicorn. The server log says why it fell back to Python.

steps.title: Observability
steps.goal: Every request gets an ID, a timing header and one structured log line; /metrics shows counters.
concepts: Request IDs connect a client's error report to your server logs. Reuse an incoming X-Request-ID so the ID spans services.
Structured (JSON) logs are queryable in CloudWatch Logs Insights / ELK, e.g. filter status >= 500.
The three pillars: logs (what happened), metrics (how much / how fast), traces (where time went across services).
Middleware order matters: observability wraps rate limiting, so even 429s get IDs and log lines.

steps.title: HTTPS & WSS
steps.goal: Serve the same app over TLS with a self-signed certificate.
concepts: TLS gives confidentiality, integrity and server identity. HTTPS = HTTP over TLS; WSS = WebSocket over TLS.
The client checks the cert chains to a trusted CA and matches the hostname (SAN). Self-signed certs fail that unless you trust them explicitly.
verify=False 'fixes' errors by turning off the protection. Pass the cert as a CA file instead.
In AWS you usually terminate TLS at the load balancer (ALB + ACM certificate) or API Gateway, not in uvicorn.

checks.name: GET /health over https://
checks.hint: python scripts/make_cert.py, then: uvicorn app.main:app --port 8443 --ssl-keyfile certs/key.pem --ssl-certfile certs/cert.pem, then: python cli.py --base-url https://127.0.0.1:8443 --cafile certs/cert.pem check 10

steps.title: Automated tests & CI
steps.goal: pytest suite + C++ tests + lint, run by GitHub Actions on Linux and Windows for every push.
concepts: Test pyramid: many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests (TestClient hits the real app in-process), few end-to-end.
Fixtures give each test a fresh app with an in-memory DB: no shared state, order-independent.
CI = every push builds and tests automatically. CD = passing builds deploy automatically (or with one approval).
A matrix build (ubuntu + windows) catches platform bugs: paths, line endings, DLL vs .so.

steps.title: Containerize & deploy (AWS)
steps.goal: Docker image + a deployment story you can explain on a whiteboard.
concepts: Dockerfile: multi-stage build compiles the C++ in one stage and copies only the .so into a slim runtime image.
Container options on AWS: ECS Fargate behind an ALB (long-running, WebSockets OK), or Lambda + API Gateway (bursty, pay-per-request, 15-min limit).
Data: DynamoDB (key-value/document, partition key = station, sort key = observed_at) or DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible).
Pipeline: GitHub Actions -> build image -> push to ECR -> deploy to ECS (rolling or blue/green) -> health checks gate traffic.
Config via env vars; secrets via Secrets Manager; logs to CloudWatch.
